mappings.note: A smallholder's answer to unviable machinery is to diversify into poultry, beekeeping and fruit trees - a household livelihood strategy. Goal-level CG-SST4 (socio-economic role of institutions and contributions of sections of society); no LO reaches farm economics.

Identifies Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana as the crop insurance scheme - the state acting on farmers' risk. C-SST4.2-LO-2 is rejected because that LO is a field report on a State government office in one's locality, not a central scheme.

Assertion-reason on the Ganga losing its ability to replenish through glacier melt, groundwater pumping and dams. Water conservation (LO-3); LO-2 is rejected because obstruction and over-abstraction, not contamination, carry the reason.

Distinguishes terracing (steps cut into the hill) from contour ploughing (following natural curves), both erosion controls. LO-3 conservation, not C-SST1.1-LO-2, which would be about how the slope itself formed.
Sorts the real gains of multiple cropping - harvest security, staggered yields, lower pest risk - from the claim that it removes the need for water. Land-and-water husbandry, LO-3.

Afforestation defined through its soil-conservation function: tree roots anchoring ground against erosion. LO-3 names conservation of flora alongside soil-holding; LO-2 is rejected as no pollutant is involved.

Kallanai, the Kaveri anicut built by Karikala some 1,800 years ago. A historical public work; goal-level CG-SST2 because C-SST2.2-LO-1 is confined to temples, tombs and mosques and cannot take hydraulic engineering.
Tests that Phad in Maharashtra and bamboo drip in the northeast work by gravity and manual ingenuity, not motor pumps. Water conservation through traditional systems, LO-3.
Panchagavya identified as a fermented mixture of five cow products used as biofertiliser. LO-3 conservation of soil fertility by natural input; LO-2 rejected as nothing is being decontaminated.

Sikkim's 2014 ban on chemical fertilisers and pesticides. Same two codes as the earlier Sikkim MCQ in this chapter, deliberately: the ban is a listed anti-contamination measure (LO-2) taken as a conservation commitment (LO-3).

One-word recall of the Latin root 'agri'. No LO covers the vocabulary or nature of the discipline; cited at CG-SST4, the goal that frames agriculture as economic activity. A real frame gap, not a fit.
Recall of the 46 percent workforce share. Livelihood statistic for a section of society, goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers agricultural employment.

Recall that over 75 percent of rural agricultural workers are women. C-SST4.1-LO-1 rather than goal level, because the textbook point is precisely that this labour goes unrecognised - a consequence of women's disadvantage.
Names Kalibangan as the Harappan site where intercropping evidence was found - site-based archaeological recall. Goal-level CG-SST2; no LO covers early agriculture.
Names Vrikshayurveda as the text on seed preparation and soil cultivation. A historical source question; goal-level CG-SST2, as above.
Recall of fifteen agroclimatic zones - the distribution and extent of climatic regions in India (C-SST1.2-LO-1). LO-2 rejected: nothing is inferred about how people live.

Identifies the southwest monsoon as the June-September rain-bringer, the mechanism behind the kharif season in this chapter. LO-2 rather than LO-1, since the monsoon is being tied to the farming calendar, not located on a map.
Recall of kharif, rabi and zaid. Climate-to-cropping, LO-2.
The estimate of 2,300 farmers leaving agriculture daily under debt and crop failure. Agrarian distress as a socio-economic fact; goal-level CG-SST4, no LO reaches it.
Sensor-equipped drones used to assess soil moisture. Cited to LO-3 as water-and-input efficiency, on the same reasoning as the drip-irrigation items; the frame has no LO for farm technology as such.
A hectare as 10,000 square metres, taught here to make the shrinking average holding intelligible. Goal-level CG-SST4 for the landholding context; no LO covers measurement units.
46 percent of the workforce against roughly 18 percent of GDP - the sector's weight in livelihoods versus output. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers sectoral economics.

Identifies intercropping among threshing, grafting and hydroponics. Same code as the earlier intercropping definition item for consistency: a land-husbandry practice under LO-3, with the Harappan evidence only corroborating antiquity.
Barley and millet cultivation at Mehrgarh in the seventh millennium BCE. Archaeological evidence; goal-level CG-SST2, as no LO covers early agriculture.

Assigns the Thar Desert to the arid climate and the high Himalaya to the alpine zone - naming climatic regions and their extent, C-SST1.2-LO-1. LO-2 rejected because no consequence for people is drawn.
How the southwest monsoon specifically aids farmers, answered through kharif cropping in northern India. Climate to livelihood, LO-2.

Traces kharif, rabi and zaid to Arabic and to usage since Mughal times. A question about historical terminology, so CG-SST2 at goal level rather than C-SST1.2-LO-2, which would need the seasons' climatic content.

Humus as decomposed organic matter that holds moisture and supplies nutrients - a constituent of soil. C-SST1.1-LO-1 covers the materials of the earth's surface; LO-2 would require a landform to be forming.

Red soil from weathered lava and old rock, reddened by iron. Identity and composition of a soil type, LO-1 - the same code as the earlier red-soil MCQ; the parent-rock link is what is scored, not the process.
Black soil's fertility and moisture retention traced to weathered volcanic rock, hence cotton. Soil-and-parent-rock identification, LO-1.
Multiple cropping as risk reduction and assured harvest from one field. Land husbandry, LO-3.
Contour ploughing along hill curves to avoid rain-driven erosion. Soil conservation, LO-3.
Phad as a community-managed canal system diverting river water in Maharashtra. Water conservation through a shared traditional institution, LO-3.
Sprinkler irrigation described as artificial rain over the crop - an irrigation-efficiency method. LO-3.
How the ancient seed drill saved labour by combining three operations. Historical technology; goal-level CG-SST2, since C-SST2.2-LO-1 admits only temples, tombs and mosques.

Asks for the defining features of contemporary agriculture - mechanisation, purchased inputs, market dependence. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers the character of the sector. (Model answer on this row is truncated mid-sentence by a watermark; see report.)

The clearest source-criticism item in the chapter: what Arthashastra, Vrikshayurveda and Brihat Samhita let us know about early practice. CG-SST2's goal statement covers how historians use different types of sources, but none of its competencies does, so goal level is the honest citation.
Fifteen zones defined by climate, soil and vegetation (extent and distribution, LO-1) and used to plan regional agriculture (climate shaping livelihoods, LO-2). Both strands are in the model answer.

Soil formation over millennia by physical and chemical weathering of bedrock plus organic decay. Cited to LO-2 as a formation process, matching the weathering MCQ; LO-1 is for identifying a soil or rock, which this does not ask.
Significance of crop rotation in preventing nutrient exhaustion. Soil conservation, LO-3.
Drip irrigation evaluated on minimal water wastage. Water conservation, LO-3.

The Green Revolution's effect on food security - HYV seeds, fertilisers and machinery raising grain output. Goal-level CG-SST4 for a state programme's socio-economic result; the ecological counterpart is mapped to C-SST1.3 separately, which is why these two do not share codes.
Ecological cost of the Green Revolution: pesticide and fertiliser contamination of groundwater (LO-2) plus long-term loss of soil fertility (LO-3). Both cited because the answer turns on the pair.
Organic farming's principles: compost, seed cake and manure in place of synthetic fertiliser and pesticide. LO-3 for the conservation stance, LO-2 for the avoidance of chemical contamination.
Kerala's below-sea-level saline paddy combined with fisheries and livestock - a farming life that only that terrain and climate produce. LO-2 rather than LO-1, which would stop at locating it.

Subsidised irrigation power, assisted access to seed and fertiliser, and crop insurance - the state's financial role in farming. Goal-level CG-SST4; C-SST4.2-LO-2 is a locality field report, not national policy.
Economic consequences of holdings averaging three-quarters of a hectare: low income and machinery that cannot pay for itself. Goal-level CG-SST4, no LO for agrarian economics.
Income diversification into livestock, apiculture and fishing as household resilience. Goal-level CG-SST4; the allied-activity content here is economic, not ecological, so C-SST1.3-LO-3 is rejected.

Climate change threatening agriculture through erratic monsoons and more frequent drought and torrential rain. LO-1 takes the drought-and-flood extremes it names; C-SST1.2-LO-2 takes the monsoon-dependence of farming that the threat operates on.
Ganga basin stressors: glacier melt, diversion for irrigation, dams. Water conservation, LO-3; LO-2 rejected because the model answer argues flow loss, not contamination.
Case study resolving a Punjab farmer's year into kharif, the June-September monsoon and rabi wheat. Climate-to-cropping throughout, LO-2.

Case study on Maharashtra's black soil: part (b) asks the soil's identity and why it suits cotton (LO-1), part (a) asks for the name of the rock-breakdown process (LO-2). Both parts are scored, so both codes.
Case study contrasting terracing plus panchagavya with the Green Revolution's chemicals. LO-3 for erosion control and soil health, LO-2 for the explicit avoidance of toxic synthetic inputs.

Case study on a Gujarat village: drip irrigation adopted as groundwater falls (LO-3), with part (a) requiring the name of Munsar Lake built by Queen Minaldevi centuries ago - a historical water work, hence goal-level CG-SST2 since no LO admits it.
Case study on a smallholder ruined by untimely torrential rain and rescued by crop insurance. CG-SST4 for the holding size and the state scheme; C-SST1.3-LO-1 for the extreme-rainfall event itself.
Names the three Green Revolution inputs. Goal-level CG-SST4 as a state programme's content, consistent with the other Green Revolution achievement items; its harms are mapped to C-SST1.3 instead.
The Green Revolution's primary benefit, food self-sufficiency in wheat and rice. Goal-level CG-SST4.
Two harms named: soil impoverishment (LO-3) and pesticide contamination of water (LO-2). Deliberately different codes from the benefit items above, since the question tests the ecological side.

How Sikkim moved to sustainable agriculture. LO-3 alone here, unlike the two Sikkim MCQs: this stem asks for the transition as a conservation choice, not for the ban as a measure against chemical contamination.
Kerala's integrated below-sea-level system. Region-specific farming life, LO-2.
